recipes.name: Mama's Asian Chicken and Rice
ingredients_raw: 1.5 pounds skinless, boneless chicken breast halves, cubed

steps.text: In a bowl, stir together warm water, brown sugar, orange juice, soy sauce, ketchup, white vinegar, garlic, red pepper flakes, five-spice powder, and orange peel until the sugar has dissolved and the mixture is well combined.

Heat the olive oil in a large skillet or wok over medium heat, and cook and stir the chicken until the outside is golden brown and the inside is no longer pink, 10 to 12 minutes. Pour the sauce mixture over the chicken, bring to a boil, reduce heat to medium-low, and cover the skillet. Simmer for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.

While the chicken and sauce are simmering, bring the rice and water to a boil in a saucepan over high heat. Reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until the rice is tender, and the liquid has been absorbed, 20 to 25 minutes. Set the rice aside and keep warm.

Whisk the cornstarch and 2 tablespoons of cold water in a small bowl until smooth, and stir into the chicken and sauce, a few teaspoons at a time. Let the chicken and sauce cook for about 2 minutes to thicken, then serve over hot cooked rice, sprinkled with green onion.

raw_recipe.headline: Mama's Asian Chicken and Rice
raw_recipe.description: Chunks of boneless chicken breast simmer with an Asian-inspired sweet, tangy orange sauce, and are served over hot cooked rice with a sprinkling of green onions.

video.description: Zesty orange chicken with rice will amaze you by how full-flavored and well-balanced the sauce is. Add in some veggies for a perfect meal.

review.reviewBody: We enjoyed this dish. I took other's advice and doubled the sauce, ( I didn't double the red pepper flakes, though). Should have went with my gut and not used as much cornstarch slurry as it called for. I doubled it since I doubled the sauce and it was very thick and not very sauce like. Next time will slowly add in cornstarch slurry until I like the consistancy. I will make this again as it was quick and easy! Served with green beans and eggrolls.
I made this mostly based on the recipe, only thing was I used the juice of the whole orange and coating the chicken before cooking with corn starch for crispness. It was amazing!!! Sooo good.

Amazing and simple. I’m not good doing comments but since I did this with chicken thighs thought I should comment. I grilled some fresh chicken thighs a couple days earlier instead of freezing them. Loosely followed the recipe, cut the brown sugar in half and kept the corn starch the same. Used sesame oil and added sesame seeds. Sautéed in the sauce only five minutes or so because the the thighs were already cooked. Still amazing. Paired with sticky rice and added red pepper afterward (because I forgot it). Added a little fish sauce. Amazing! Seems like the kind of recipe you can fudge and still really good. Easy peasy and even better the next day

Yummy! I’ve been holding on to this recipe for a few months and finally made it tonight. I thought there would be leftovers, but I was wrong. Everyone in my family loved it! I followed the ingredients to the letter, but did double the sauce as other reviewers suggested. I’m glad I did because we served it over rice and the sauce was a great addition. As other reviewers suggested, I did marinate the chicken in a mixture of orange juice and soy sauce the night before I made it. I drained the marinade well before sautéing. After sautéing the chicken I took it out of the pan and set it aside. I poured the sauce in the same pan and brought it to a very low boil, stirring constantly for 3-5 minutes. The sauce reduced and thickened with out adding the corn starch. Once the sauce was think, I turned off the cooktop tossed the chicken back in to coat and served over rice with broccoli on the side.
Thanks for a great recipe!
Rice vinegar, onions, green/ red peppers-sliced, less brown sugar, 2Tbls Sesame oil. Good recipe. Thank you!

2018/2019 ... https://www.allrecipes.com/recipe/214043/mamas-asian-chicken-and-rice/ ... 
For the listed amount of chicken, double the sauce & the rice. I subbed chicken broth for the water. Since no Chinese five spice, again this is the doubled amount to make 1/2t: 1/4 anise extract, 1/4t ground cinnamon, 1/16t ground cloves. Oh, no orange peel added & reduced the crushed red pepper to 3/4t. I went with coating chicken cubes with cornstarch, about 1/4c, rather than thickening the sauce. Coating keeps the chicken moist & cooks slightly crispy. I only browned the chicken then simmered until cooked. The sauce was thickened & the chicken was cooked in fifteen minutes. Pretty nice. ;) I stirred in a bit of sesame oil. Very slight orange flavor & medium-heat spice.

My husband and I LOVE it!

I've referenced this recipe for years, particularly for the sauce, which is outstanding. I've made a few changes to the steps.

1. Marinate the cut up chicken in OJ for a couple of hours. The citrus makes it more tender and juicy.
2. Prepare the sauce as directed in a small sauce pan, over low heat.
3. Remove the chicken from the marinade, dredge it in cornstarch (or cornstarch / flour mixture) and pan fry in oil of your choice. Cornstarch gives it a crispy result.
4. Drain the fried chicken pieces onto a paper towel, then turn on to a serving dish.
5. Meanwhile, increase temperature on your sauce. Whisk a little cornstarch with water and stir it into the sauce. Stir until thickened.
6. Pour hot sauce over meat, give it a quick stir and serve.

I did not have Chinese Five Spice, so I googled a substitute, and used a mix of ground cinnamon, ground cloves, ground ginger and ground anise instead. Also, cut up some pineapple and several of us liked it mixed in. I also made a separate batch with veggies for the vegetarians in our house (what I had on hand: onions, green peppers, carrots, celery, and water chestnuts). It was equally as incredible. I opted to mix some of the veggies in with mine as well, and that was terrific! Definitely making this again!

Very good sauce. I basically just made the recipe for the sauce alone. I had leftover chicken from a large roaster, so I did not need to cook chicken breast first. I doubled the sauce recipe as many had suggested and just let it simmer down for 20-30 minutes until the majority of the water had evaporated off. I made a few changes, with reducing the red pepper, I did not have orange zest, and I added a drop of both ginger and tangerine oil. Once the sauce was cooked down, I tossed the cooked chicken, a bag of cooked Asian style vegetables, and a handful of cashews, and let it heat through. Served everything over ramen noodles. It tasted as good as delivery!

I've made this twice now and it was a big hit both times. As someone recommended, I made extra sauce (about 1.5x the recipe) and I think it's about perfect. One other thing, use paper towels to pat as much moisture as you can from the chicken before cooking. If you don't, you just end up boiling the chicken and the water never cooks off.
Really straight forward and time efficient to make. I added some freshly ground ginger, which add some flavor depth to the dish.
This turned out to be an amazing meal! I doubled the sauce and added onions and peppers.
A little more OJ I think. Added some steamed broccoli before serving.

Made it as written, although was probably a little heavy on the orange zest. Sauce had a good flavor, orange came through nicely and the pepper flakes added just the right heat. Found that the chicken gave off lots of juice, which combined with the sauce made just the right quantity. This might be the reason some people need to increase the sauce. Will probably add some veggies to the next batch.
It came out perfect and I'm saving this recipe for later since everyone loves it. I did read the comments and doubled the orange juice though. I think doubling the OJ was essential.
I might tweak a couple of spices in the future
Very good! Actually made the chicken portion to meal prep, and it actually seemed more flavorful after 2 days in the fridge.

Super simple and taste yummy!!! And it looks amazing! It's also very easy to alter if needed. I didn't have orange so used lemon juice instead and did not use any peel. I doubled the sauce portion as well. 10/10

It was good, but very sweet and a strong orange flavor. I think I might add less orange juice/peel next time. It was very quick and easy to make. This was 2 portions as I used 2 chicken breasts and there was enough sauce for 2 of us.
